consequence: The ensemble bundle's digest changed, so it no longer matches the activation made before the release. A re-activation is required before the desks launch, so the running field binds the code it actually runs -- the same discipline A13 records failing to observe.
defect: The equal-risk ensemble lets a member that holds contribute the book it last emitted, so that a hold means 'no change to my book' rather than 'I have no book'. The Top-50 universe rotates weekly, so a stale book can still name a symbol that has since left the eligible cross-section, and the ensemble averaged and emitted it. A lane strategy never meets this because it rebuilds from the current section at every decision; an ensemble that reuses books has to prune them.
design_note: The hold-carries-its-last-book rule is still right: treating a hold as flat would quietly de-risk the ensemble every time a member went quiet. The bug was in what that carried book may contain, not in carrying it.
fix: The ensemble intersects the averaged book with context.eligible_symbols before emitting. Verified live by mutation: reverting the filter fails exactly the new test.
found_at_phase: after release, before the paper desks launched
found_by: the evaluator's own eligibility guard, during the ensemble's launch-state reconstruction: 'strategy targeted ineligible symbol FLMUSDT'
no_tournament_result_is_affected: The ensemble is a forward-stage desk, not a competitor. It has no leaderboard entry, no nomination and no score; it was never observed on the sealed window and could not have been. The release and every rank in it stand untouched.
title: the ensemble emitted a symbol that had left the universe
why_the_guard_is_right: Emitting a departed symbol is a candidate failure and correctly so. The evaluator force-settles a name on its way out of the universe and will not let a strategy re-enter it, because a book that keeps trading a delisted or demoted contract is not a book that could have been traded.
